summary: Three small faults in changes this branch made itself, mended in one commit. (1) Dead keys. `Finder::check_filter_field` (src/finder/filter.rs) is called first thing in `Render for Finder::render` (src/finder/mod.rs, right after `rename_frame_started`): when the filter bar isn't showing and its field has the keyboard, the files take it, before anything of the browser is drawn, so that same frame is drawn with the files focused and no other frame is asked for. That is where the keyboard ended up when a dialog opened from a Smart Folder's filter field gave it back after the bar had gone under it: Go to Folder confirmed with Return, or `fff gui`/a second launch (`open_request`) with any dialog open over that field. (2) Relevance chosen again. `Finder::set_sort` (src/finder/mod.rs) returns at once when the key is Relevance and Relevance is the current key: no direction is turned around and no search runs again. (3) Swallowed clicks. The capture-phase guard on the file area for the buttons under its message (`message_button_clicked`, in `render_content`) clears its flag at the first left press on the file area whatever its count, stops only a press counted second or later, and records that press through the new `Presses::left_alone()` (src/finder/views.rs) so the views don't leave the next press alone as well. The guard stays: without its stop the second press of a double-click presses the next button and toggles a group's header, which `Presses` doesn't cover. docs/manual.md: the Sort By line says Relevance, chosen again, has no order to reverse.
changelog: (No entry: a fault in an unreleased change.) Go to Folder confirmed with Return from the filter field of an open Smart Folder left every key the window handles dead until a click, choosing Relevance again in a search's Sort menu checked Descending beside two disabled directions and searched a cut list again, and after a double-click on a button under the file area's message every further click made without a pause or a move of the mouse was ignored.
behaviour_changes: Go to Folder (Cmd+Shift+G; Ctrl+Shift+G or Ctrl+L elsewhere) called with the keyboard in the filter field of an open Smart Folder whose filter is as the Smart Folder set it, and confirmed with Return: the files have the keyboard afterwards. Before, the arrow keys, typing, Cmd+F, Cmd+Shift+G and the other shortcuts the window handles did nothing until something was clicked. Tested; run again in review for a folder, for the folder the Smart Folder itself searches (the brief's own steps, with and without nu), and for a file's path (its folder shows with the file selected, drawn in the active colour: pictured).

The same when the window is sent elsewhere (`fff gui PATH`, a second launch) while any dialog opened from that field is up, and the dialog is then closed with Escape or its close button. Tested with Search Syntax and Escape.

How: as each frame starts, a browser whose filter field has the keyboard while its filter bar isn't showing gives the keyboard to its files. For the 250 ms the kit takes to give the keyboard back after Return, keys still go nowhere, as after any dialog.

Unchanged: a dialog that leaves the bar where it is gives the keyboard back to the filter field and typing goes on in it (tested for a Smart Folder's bar with Escape; probed in review for the window's own bar with Return, with text in it and empty). A Smart Folder's filter edited by hand keeps its bar when the search ends, so after Go to Folder and Return the keyboard is in that field again, as before (probed in review). The Go button, the Back button's menu and Actions > Filter with Nushell from that field were fine before and still are (the implementer's probes). In split view only the pane concerned takes the keyboard (the implementer's probe).

Choosing Relevance again, the checked item, in a search's Sort menu or the empty-space menu's Sort By, by mouse or by keys: nothing happens. Before, Descending became the checked direction beside two disabled items (pictured), and a list whose items a sort may choose (the `+` in the status bar) was searched again: spinner, rows replaced, and a selected row that dropped out lost its selection.

After a double-click on a button under the file area's message (Search This Computer, Search Any Kind, Remove Filter) only the second press is ignored. The third click at that spot is a first click: it selects the item now under the pointer, or clears the selection in empty space, and the fourth opens the item. Before, every further click made without a pause or a move of the mouse was ignored. Tested; probed in review with both clicks of the double-click sent before any frame and before the search answered.

New with that: when the next button has come under the pointer, the third click presses it (before: ignored until the mouse rested). Search Any Kind saves Any as the kind. When a group's header has come under the pointer, the second press still does nothing and the third toggles the group (the implementer's probe).
After one click on such a button, a later press in the file area that the system counts second or later is ignored once, as before, but no longer keeps the clicks after it ignored.
Manual, Sort and View Options, Sort By: "Choosing the current key again reverses the order, except for Relevance, which has none to reverse."
left_out: No `window.defer(.. window.refresh())` after the draw-time check, which the proposal asked for. The keyboard is moved before anything of the browser reads it, and GPUI records a frame's focus as the file area is laid out, so the frame is drawn with the files focused. Checked in review by reading every read of the focus in src (all are inside the browser's own render, after the call; the workspace reads none) and in a picture; see notes for what a later reader outside the browser has to mind.

The draw-time net was chosen over the proposal's narrower alternative (giving the files the keyboard in `focus_before_dialog` when a Smart Folder is open). That one would take the keyboard from the filter field after every cancelled dialog and would not cover `fff gui`.

No kept test with the dialogs' animations on (it needs real sleeps), for the dialog's close button, for split view, for Remove Filter in the four views, or for a group's header under the pointer: the implementer's probes, in /home/user/polish-tools/shots/fix-own-small-faults-probes.rs.txt. The review's own are in fix-own-small-faults-review-probes.rs.txt beside it.
`fff show` (`show_results`) and Connect to Server confirmed with Return from that field were not run. They reach the same `navigate` -> `end_search` path.

A tab that isn't showing isn't rendered, so the net doesn't run for it. Nothing hands a hidden tab's filter field the keyboard today: no key reaches the tabs under a dialog, the dialog's backdrop takes the presses, and `open_request` goes to the tab that shows.
`replace_filter`'s own hand-off of the keyboard is now spare for the frame after it, and left as it is: it acts at once.
No pictures of the double-click fault: shot.sh can't send counted clicks. The tests and probes cover it.
CHANGELOG.md is not edited (the guide, and the orchestrator's note that this gets no entry). The commit says `Changelog: none (fixes a fault in an unreleased change).`

`cargo clippy --features term` not run: src/term is untouched and nothing it calls changed (grepped again in review, with src/macos.rs, src/win.rs, src/server, src/workspace.rs and src/lib.rs). Nothing was compiled for macOS or Windows; the diff has no cfg-specific code and changes no signature.
README.md and the Search Syntax dialog: neither states anything this changes. The manual's Double-click row and its paragraph on which part has the keyboard already say what now happens.

review_fixes: The comment on `Finder::check_filter_field` said that GPUI reports nothing lost when the keyboard lands on a field that isn't drawn, so `keyboard_lost` can't be the one to act. Probed, that holds only for Return, where the kit gives the keyboard back a quarter second after the dialog went. For Escape, the close button and a click beside the dialog the kit gives it back at once, and `keyboard_lost` is then called in the very frame the keyboard is on the undrawn field, with no restore target (what went was the dialog), and returns at its first line. The comment now says what the commit message already said: what stopped being drawn with the keyboard was the dialog, no part of this browser, and nothing is reported when the keyboard then lands on the field. It also says now that the files take the keyboard before anything of the browser is drawn and that no other frame is asked for, which is why the call has to stay first in `render`.
Nothing else in src, in the tests or in the manual was changed in review. I looked for a reason to and did not find one; the doubts that remain are under notes.
The lane held the implementer's commit 4ff4f82 on the trunk's tip ddefe96; the trunk had not moved by the time of the push, so the rebase was a no-op. The trunk commit is ffb02de.
notes:
Checked. With the commit's src diff reverse-applied the three new UI tests fail, each for the brief's reason (a search in flight after Relevance is chosen again; the files without the keyboard after Return; the third click selecting nothing), and their two neighbours pass; applied again, `git status` was clean. The unit test went with the diff, so I ran three mutations of the final code one at a time: the guard's stop taken out fails a_double_click_on_a_button_under_no_results_doesnt_press_the_next_one and the second half of the new test (kind Any, not Folder) while ..._opens_nothing passes, which is the evidence that the guard is still needed; `left_alone()` recording nothing fails the unit test and the new UI test; the old rule (the flag cleared only at a first-counted press) fails the new UI test. The seven tests around the change pass with SEED=3, 11, 2024 and 77777. check.sh printed CHECK OK on the trunk commit's tree: 815 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures. Pushed to origin (ddefe96..ffb02de). I looked at the window myself: the Smart Folder with the keyboard in its filter field; then Go to Folder with a file's path and Return, nothing pressed after it: the bar is gone and the file is selected in the active colour; the same steps on the source without the change show it grey, and a Down Arrow after it moves nothing, where with the change it moves to the next item; and the Sort menu after Relevance was chosen again, with Ascending still the checked direction.

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt someone, and what the code and the runs say. (1) The draw-time net takes the keyboard from a field someone is typing in, leaves a frame drawn with the old state, or keeps drawing. I had `check_filter_field` write a line to a file whenever it moves the keyboard and ran every test: it fired twice, both in the new dialog test, and in none of the other 814, among them the tests that open and close the bar, type in it, open dialogs from it and enter and leave Smart Folders. It can act only when the field has the keyboard and the bar isn't drawn, a state in which no key reaches anything; before the change such a state either was rescued one frame later by `keyboard_lost` (same end) or stayed dead. Every read of the focus while drawing is inside the browser's render, after the call (sidebar.rs, views.rs, toolbar.rs, tab_bar.rs; the workspace reads none), and `Window::focus` asks for no frame while a frame is drawn, so there is one frame and no loop (the implementer's probe: a listener for the files getting the keyboard fires once). With the window's own bar open, Return in Go to Folder gives the keyboard back to the field and typing goes on (probed). (2) A click that was ignored now does something nobody aimed at. The third click after a double-click on a message button is a click again: on an item it selects, and the fourth opens it, which is what the brief asks; on the next button it presses it; on a group's header it toggles the group. That is the rule stray-double-click set for a dialog's buttons, and the orchestrator's pointer (clear the flag at the first left press whatever its count). See doubt (a). (3) A real double-click that stops working, or Relevance left in a state with no way out. The flag is now cleared by any left press on the file area, so a flag left standing can stop only a press counted second or later whose first press was not a left press on this file area: the rest of a double-click on something else, which the views leave alone on an item anyway, and one press only. A double-click on an item begins with a press counted first on the file area, which clears the flag. `set_sort(Relevance)` is reachable only from the Sort menu and the empty-space menu's Sort By, only while searching; a search starts at Relevance ascending and nothing else can turn that direction around now, so the early return cannot strand a list at Relevance descending.

Doubts that remain, for the owner. (a) A triple click on Search This Computer now presses Search Any Kind with its third click when that button has come under the pointer (a search limited to a folder and to a kind that finds nothing on This Computer either), and Search Any Kind saves Any as the kind. Before this change the third and later clicks did nothing until the mouse rested or moved. If the next button should need a pause, the guard is the place, and the second half of a_double_click_on_a_button_under_no_results_holds_up_no_click_after_it turns around. (b) No further frame is asked for after the net moves the keyboard, where the proposal wanted one. Nothing needs it today. (c) With a Smart Folder's filter edited by hand, Go to Folder and Return keep the bar and give the keyboard back to its field (a part changed by hand stays as changed), so letters typed next go into the filter, not to the files. Unchanged by this commit, and no key is dead. (d) For the 250 ms the kit waits after Return before it gives the keyboard back, no key reaches anything, as after any dialog confirmed with Return; and from reading the kit (gpui-component-0.8.1 src/root.rs, `defer_close_dialog`) it gives the keyboard back then even when a click has put it somewhere else in the meantime. With this change it then goes to the files where the handle is the undrawn filter field. Not run. (e) Nothing ran on macOS or Windows.

For briefs still to come.
- split-active-pane: `Render for Finder::render` now begins `self.rename_frame_started(); self.check_filter_field(window, cx);`. The second line may move the keyboard from this pane's filter field to its files while the frame is being built, and asks for no other frame. Your plan syncs `split_active` at the top of `Workspace::render` from `contains_focused` on each pane: in the one frame where the net fires, the keyboard is on a field that isn't drawn when the workspace renders, so neither pane contains it and `split_active` has to stay as it was (the plan's 'exactly one of' does that; don't fall back to the first pane when neither does). Anything drawn outside the panes that shows where the keyboard is would be one frame behind there; ask for a frame (`window.defer(cx, |window, _| window.refresh())`, as `keyboard_lost` does) if you add such a thing. The file area's guard for the message buttons stops one press in the capture phase, as the guard for rows left behind does: a capture listener registered later in the frame (the other pane's `press_capture`, anything the workspace draws after the pane) does not hear that press; the pane's own `press_capture` has heard it. The new tests press no Tab.
- inactive-selection-colour: `let active = self.files_focused(window)` in `render_icons` and `render_gallery` is read after the net has run, like the list's, so a selection is drawn active in the first frame after a dialog gave the keyboard back to a filter bar that went (pictured here for the list: fix-own-small-faults-review-2-after-return.png, and grey without the change). Keep `check_filter_field` before anything in `render` that reads the focus.
- idle-redraw-after-search: the net asks for no frame and notifies nothing. In each frame it costs two field reads while the bar is open, and otherwise a focus handle's clone and a compare. It moves the keyboard once each time the kit hands it to the undrawn field.
- go-to-folder-keyboard: the_files_get_the_keyboard_when_a_dialog_gives_it_back_to_a_filter_bar_that_went types the fixture's root, an absolute path that exists, into Go to Folder and presses Return, and expects `ui.folder() == fx.dir` with the dialog closed; your order (a selected row, else the typed path if it exists, else the only match) keeps that. Return closes through the kit's hand-back a quarter second later, the Go button through `window.close_dialog` and `focus_files`. If you make Return close like the Go button, the first part of the test passes for another reason, and the net stays pinned by the second part (`open_request` under Search Syntax, then Escape). The field under the dialog needs no hand-off of your own. Its third part opens Go to Folder from the filter field and presses Escape with nothing typed, then types 0 into the filter: Escape has to close the dialog at the first press there.
- collapsible-sidebar-sections: the new dialog test clicks `("smart", 0usize)` three times in a new window, so the Smart Folders section has to start open.
- fix-wording-after-later-changes: the manual's Sort By line (Sort and View Options) now ends 'Choosing the current key again reverses the order, except for Relevance, which has none to reverse.' The Double-click row of Selecting items and the paragraph at the top of Keyboard shortcuts ('When the part that has the keyboard goes away, the file views get it') were true to the words before and are now true in these cases too; nothing to reword for this change.
- fix-filter-reruns-and-fresh-rows (lane-e, in progress), filter-stale-keep-set: `check_filter_field` sits in src/finder/filter.rs between `replace_filter` and `open_smart_folder` and reads only `filter_bar_open()` and the field's focus handle. If a filter that runs again ever closes the bar and opens it again, the field must not hold the keyboard across a frame without its bar: the net would give the keyboard to the files in that frame. Nothing does that today (`filter_open` changes only in `toggle_filter`, `close_filter` and `replace_filter`).
- fix-rename-press-selection (lane-c, in progress): independent. A name's field in the views ends its edit in the capture phase of a press from a listener inside the file area, and the message-button guard, registered on the file area itself, runs before it. But the guard stops a press only as the rest of a double-click on a button under the message: when that button was clicked no row was drawn, so no name was being edited in the views, and the click ended one being edited in the sidebar's tree.
- context-menus-fit, icon-tile-hit-target: the tests for a double-click on a button under No Results (three now) find the row under the button's centre in the list view, by `item_id("row", path)`, among 60 files in a window of the default size, and need Search Any Kind to be the one button left where part of Search This Computer was. None of them is in the icon view.
- regex-content-search, recent-searches: `set_sort(SortKey::Relevance)` does nothing when Relevance is the current key, and from any other key puts the results back in relevance order as before. A contents search was never searched again for a sort.
- restore-session-tabs: a tab that never showed has never been rendered, so its net has not run; nothing gives such a tab's filter field the keyboard.
- quick-look-empty-state: in `--term` mode Quick Look is a dialog in the same window; opened over a Smart Folder's filter field it gives the keyboard back like any dialog, and the net covers the field if its bar went meanwhile.
- type-select-space, view-switch-keeps-selection, select-all-perf, tree-arrows-past-smart-folder, multi-word-highlights, content-match-highlight, preview-page-keys, search-start-no-flash and the rest: independent. In tests/controls.rs the three new tests sit after a_sort_chooses_among_every_match_not_among_the_ones_listed, after a_double_click_on_a_button_under_no_results_opens_nothing, and after the_keyboard_stays_in_the_window_when_a_smart_folder_takes_the_filter_bar_away; in src/finder/views.rs `Presses::left_alone` is between `in_empty_space` and `forget`, and its unit test after the_click_after_one_that_was_left_alone_is_a_first_click.

Found, not fixed (all there before this change, outside this brief).
- The Sort menu begins with the label 'Sort By', and the kit's first Down Arrow in a menu selects index 0, the label, so Return then does nothing and it takes a second Down to reach the first sort key (the implementer: seen in the harness and in the screenshot example; read in gpui-component-0.8.1 src/menu/popup_menu.rs `select_down`).
- The kit gives the keyboard back a quarter second after a dialog is confirmed with Return, without looking whether a click has moved it since (doubt d; from reading, not run).
- A dialog that outlived a change of tab would give the keyboard back to a handle in a tab that isn't drawn, whatever it was opened from. I found no way to change tabs under a dialog.
- In a window 1100 points wide with the sidebar showing, the toolbar's title during a search is cut to 'Searching…': the words searched for are what doesn't fit (seen in the pictures of the Sort menu and of the Smart Folder).
